decisions.title: Score-level standardisation before penalised Cox
decisions.current_frozen_state: TRAINING-FOLD ONLY. Each pathway score is centred and scaled to unit variance using the mean and sample SD (ddof=1) of the TRAINING samples of that fold, applied unchanged to held-out samples. Recomputed independently inside every resampling, bootstrap and inner-CV tuning operation. Training-fold SD == 0 or <= 1e-12 -> the score is DROPPED for that fold and the exclusion recorded. A non-finite training-fold mean or SD marks the replicate NON-ESTIMABLE, recorded with its reason; never silently redrawn or substituted. The unstandardised scores are preserved unchanged as the auditable source features. This is a SECOND standardisation, applied to the scores, and does not alter the frozen gene-level standardisation (sigma_ddof=1, M2-A1) that produces them.
decisions.frozen_state_before_m2a2: NONE before the Cox model (penalisation handles scale). If added later it is training-fold-only.
options_considered: A. leave scores on their current scales (status quo)
B. standardise scores using TRAINING-FOLD mean and SD only
C. standardise and report both as a prespecified sensitivity analysis
decisions.recommendation_text: Standardise the pathway scores to unit variance using training-fold parameters only, inside every resampling boundary, and retain the unstandardised scores unchanged as the auditable source features.
rationale: The frozen justification -- 'penalisation handles scale' -- is not correct as stated. Ridge and elastic-net penalties are NOT scale-invariant: the penalty lambda*sum(beta^2) is applied per unit coefficient, so a predictor with smaller dispersion needs a larger coefficient to express the same effect and is therefore shrunk harder.
Phase 8C measured a 3x dispersion range across the five scores (SD 0.554 E2F to 0.185 PI3K). Under the current state the penalty would treat them unequally for a reason unrelated to their content.
Standardised coefficients are interpretable on a common footing -- log-hazard per 1 SD of score -- which is what a cross-pathway comparison requires.

The coherence information is NOT lost: implied within-set gene correlation is already recorded in reports/phase8c/score_distributions.csv and is reported alongside, where it belongs, rather than being smuggled into the penalty.
limitations_of_the_recommendation: Standardising deliberately removes the dispersion difference from the coefficient scale. That difference is real information about set coherence; it must be reported separately or it is simply lost.
It adds one more quantity estimated inside each fold, which adds Monte-Carlo variance and must be covered by the MC-1..MC-4 checks.
Any comparison with an unstandardised fit is not like-for-like and must not be presented as one.
Low dispersion is NOT low biological relevance. Standardisation must not be read as a claim that the five scores are equally informative; no outcome association has been tested.

scaling_guard_rules.zero_variance_score_in_a_training_fold: if the training-fold SD of a score is 0 (or < 1e-12), the standardisation is undefined. That score is DROPPED for that fold and the drop is recorded per fold -- the same convention the frozen gene-level rule already uses for zero-variance genes. It is never silently set to 0 or 1.
scaling_guard_rules.non_finite_score: a non-finite training-fold mean or SD aborts that replicate, which is recorded as a non-estimable replicate (see the validation specification) rather than being imputed away.
scaling_guard_rules.expected_frequency: neither condition is expected: Phase 8C observed 0 zero-variance genes and 0 non-finite values across 453 samples. The rules exist so the behaviour is defined, not because the conditions are anticipated.
scaling_guard_rules.recorded_in: per-fold diagnostics, reported with the model

clinical_predictor_scaling.question: does standardising the pathway scores settle the scaling of the clinical predictors?
clinical_predictor_scaling.answer: NO. It settles only the pathway block.
clinical_predictor_scaling.detail: The clinical block is four binaries plus a 2-column age spline basis on the YEAR scale. Those columns have wildly different dispersions from each other and from a standardised score, so if they are penalised they inherit exactly the scale-dependence D8D-1 is fixing -- in the opposite direction, since a large-valued basis column carries a small coefficient and is barely penalised.
clinical_predictor_scaling.resolution: this is NOT resolved inside D8D-1. It is raised as a separate decision D9-1 (penalisation scope), because the clean answer is to leave the clinical block UNPENALISED rather than to standardise it.

coefficient_interpretation_after_standar.scale: log cause-specific hazard ratio per 1 training-fold SD of the pathway score
coefficient_interpretation_after_standar.comparability: coefficients become comparable ACROSS pathways because each is expressed per its own SD
coefficient_interpretation_after_standar.what_it_does_NOT_mean: a larger standardised coefficient does NOT mean a pathway is more biologically important. Standardisation removes the dispersion difference from the coefficient scale, so the coefficient no longer carries information about how coordinated the gene set is.
coefficient_interpretation_after_standar.dispersion_vs_relevance: score dispersion is a joint property of the gene set's internal coherence and of the averaging transform (SD = 1/sqrt(k) if members were independent). A low-dispersion score such as P53 (implied inter-gene r = 0.033) is a weakly coordinated AVERAGE, which is a statement about co-expression in this tissue under this preprocessing -- NOT a statement about biological relevance and NOT a statement about recurrence, which has not been tested. Phase 8C's coherence table is reported alongside the coefficients precisely so the two are not conflated.

leakage_constraints_if_approved: mean and SD estimated on TRAINING samples only
training-derived parameters applied UNCHANGED to held-out samples
scaling recomputed independently inside EVERY resampling, bootstrap and inner-CV tuning operation -- including the inner tuning loop, not only the outer split
held-out samples never influence the scaling parameters
unstandardised scores preserved UNCHANGED as the auditable source features, written to disk and reported
zero-variance and non-finite conditions handled by the explicit rules above and recorded per fold

decisions.title: Four-set primary vs five-set sensitivity interpretation
decisions.current_frozen_state: 4-set PRIMARY, 5-set SENSITIVITY-only; PI3K may not be promoted or removed on observed performance (M2-A1)
decisions.recommendation: Adopt the reporting framework below. NO role change.
comparisons_to_be_reported: M2 primary (M1 + 4 scores) vs M1: optimism-corrected delta-C with CI and Monte-Carlo SE -- THE primary comparison
M2 sensitivity (M1 + 5 scores) vs M1: same quantities
M2 sensitivity vs M2 primary: reported as a STABILITY check, never as a selection contest
M3 exploratory vs M1: reported with its exploratory label attached
interpretation_rules_fixed_in_advance: The 4-set result is reported as primary ALWAYS, whatever the 5-set shows.
The 5-set is reported ALONGSIDE, never instead of, the 4-set.
A delta-C between the panels that lies within its Monte-Carlo SE is declared 'no evidence of a difference' -- not a tie to be broken by a second metric.
A metric improvement in the 5-set is NOT grounds to switch panels. Added flexibility and the extra parameter can improve apparent fit; that is a property of the comparison, not evidence about PI3K.
Coefficient changes for P53 and PI3K are reported together with their CIs and variance inflation, because r = 0.631 between them makes individual coefficient instability FORESEEABLE.
PI3K's descriptive redundancy (R2 = 0.540 on the primary four, Phase 8C) is stated whenever its coefficient is discussed.
Divergence is interpreted as evidence about the STABILITY of the primary estimate, not as a reason to prefer either panel.
decisions.prespecified_divergence_metric: optimism-corrected delta-C (5-set minus 4-set) with its bootstrap CI and Monte-Carlo SE, fixed before unblinding

approval.scope: panel reporting hierarchy only; no model fitting, no outcome analysis authorised

unchanged_by_this_approval: scoring definitions (sigma_ddof=1, M2-A1; score standardisation, M2-A2)
prohibitions: the 5-set panel MUST NOT be promoted to primary on the basis of model performance or statistical significance
the 4-set analysis IS the pre-specified primary result and is reported as such REGARDLESS of which panel performs better
the 5-set analysis is reported as a SENSITIVITY analysis, never as the headline result
pathway-score dispersion or correlation MUST NOT be interpreted as proof of biological activity or clinical relevance

collinearity_diagnostics.also_report: variance inflation factors and the coefficient CIs for P53 and PI3K TOGETHER

why_pi3k_is_sensitivity_only.reason: its correlation with P53 (r = 0.6314) is the only |r| > 0.5 pair in the 5-set panel and raises the condition number from 2.949 to 7.032, which makes individual coefficient instability FORESEEABLE
why_pi3k_is_sensitivity_only.explicitly_NOT_the_reason: this is NOT evidence that PI3K/AKT/mTOR is biologically irrelevant. It is a statement about the CONDITIONING of the score matrix in this cohort under this preprocessing, and nothing more. No outcome association has been tested for any pathway.

analysis_hierarchy_vs_observed_performan.rule: the reporting protocol distinguishes the PRE-SPECIFIED ANALYSIS HIERARCHY from OBSERVED MODEL PERFORMANCE. The hierarchy was fixed before any outcome was seen and does not move; performance is a result reported within it.
operationally: sensitivity result = 5-set, reported alongside and labelled
a delta-C between panels within its Monte-Carlo SE is reported as 'no evidence of a difference', not as a tie to be broken by another metric
divergence is reported transparently and read as evidence about the STABILITY of the primary estimate

decisions.title: WNT representation sensitivity
decisions.current_frozen_state: median aggregation PRIMARY; representative-IQR is the frozen sensitivity representation (A-05), and Phase 6A already registers estimand S-7 as a representative-IQR re-fit
decisions.recommendation: Do NOT create a new policy. Use the ALREADY-REGISTERED estimand S-7 (representative-IQR re-fit) and attach to it a prespecified, WNT-focused comparison.

comparison_specification.unit_of_comparison: a complete re-fit of M2 primary under the representative-IQR representation; the same pipeline, the same folds, the same seeds
quantities_compared: per-pathway standardised coefficient and its CI, pathway by pathway
optimism-corrected C-index and delta-C vs M1
rank correlation of the linear predictor between representations
the WNT coefficient specifically, since WNT is the only score whose two representations correlate below 0.9
interpretation: Agreement means the result does not depend on the probe-to-gene rule. It is NOT independent confirmation -- it is the same samples, the same genes and the same deposited matrix, summarised differently.
Disagreement confined to WNT is read as representation sensitivity of a 41-gene, low-coherence set (implied inter-gene r = 0.041), not as biology.
Disagreement across several pathways would call the representation choice itself into question and is reported as such.
comparison_specification.selection_guard: The MEDIAN representation is the primary result and is reported as primary REGARDLESS of which representation is more favourable. The representative-IQR re-fit is reported in full whatever it shows. Neither may be chosen after seeing outcomes.

approval.approved_scope: median gene representation PRIMARY vs representative-IQR SENSITIVITY -- broader than the original WNT-focused proposal, which is preserved above unchanged

prohibitions: the primary representation MUST NOT be replaced on the basis of observed model performance
the representation correlations MUST NOT be interpreted as evidence that one representation is universally superior
neither representation may be chosen after seeing outcomes
mandatory_reporting_when_the_analyses_ar: whether key conclusions are DIRECTIONALLY consistent across the two representations
any differences in pathway scores, coefficients, uncertainty, discrimination, or other relevant model outputs
the median-representation result as primary, reported in full regardless of which representation looks more favourable

representation_agreement_phase8c.metric: Pearson correlation of the pathway score between the two frozen representations, over the 453 S3 samples
representation_agreement_phase8c.acknowledgement: WNT has the WEAKEST representation agreement of the five scores (0.858) and is the only one below 0.9. It is the smallest set (41 genes) and the least internally coherent of the primary four (implied inter-gene r = 0.041), so each gene's probe choice matters more. This is acknowledged explicitly and carried into the reporting of any WNT result.
representation_agreement_phase8c.not_evidence_of_superiority: these correlations say how much the two summarisation rules AGREE. They do NOT rank the representations, and a higher correlation does not make either one more correct.

robustness_is_not_performance.statement: representation ROBUSTNESS and PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE are different properties and are reported separately, never substituted for one another.
robustness_is_not_performance.robustness: whether a conclusion survives changing the probe-to-gene summarisation rule. It is a stability property of the analysis pipeline.
robustness_is_not_performance.performance: how well a model discriminates or calibrates. It is an outcome-dependent quantity and NONE has been computed.
robustness_is_not_performance.and_neither_is_replication: agreement between representations is NOT independent replication: the same samples, the same genes and the same deposited matrix, summarised differently.

decisions.title: Batch sensitivity analysis
decisions.current_frozen_state: no batch covariate in M1/M2/M3; B-04 makes any batch correction a separate decision requiring approval
decisions.recommendation: A NARROW batch sensitivity analysis is justified, as a DIAGNOSTIC plus one stratified sensitivity model. NO batch covariate is added to M1 or M2, and batch adjustment never becomes the primary analysis.

eligible_batch_variables.combat_batch: ELIGIBLE -- 9 recovered ComBat labels; the only variable that denotes processing group
eligible_batch_variables.combat_mod: NOT ELIGIBLE -- perfectly concordant with MMR status, so adjusting for it would adjust away the dominant biological axis of the cohort
eligible_batch_variables.rna.extraction.method: NOT ELIGIBLE as an adjustment -- almost completely confounded with batch (chi2 = 2265, df = 40), min cell 14; reported descriptively only
eligible_batch_variables.dataset (discovery/validation): NOT ELIGIBLE -- Phase 1 established these are not independent cohorts; expression-level separation is negligible (eps2 <= 0.005)

design: DIAGNOSTIC 1 -- leave-one-batch-out stability: refit M2 primary nine times, each omitting one ComBat batch, and report the spread of the standardised coefficients and of delta-C. This is a stability diagnostic, not an adjusted model, and estimates no batch effect. CAVEAT, pre-registered: the batches differ ~7-fold in size (14 to 103), so omitting batch03 or batch04 removes ~23% of the cohort while omitting batch02 removes 3%. The spread therefore conflates batch identity with sample size, and the omitted n is reported beside every refit so the two are not confused.

SENSITIVITY MODEL 1 -- batch-STRATIFIED Cox: M2 primary with the baseline hazard stratified by ComBat batch, estimating NO batch coefficients. Stratification allows different baseline hazards without forcing batch to absorb biological variation through a coefficient.
Neither is run before the primary analysis, and neither can replace it.

sparse_level_handling.v1_proposal_REVERSED: Phase 9 v1.0 proposed pooling strata below 20 samples into a single 'small-batch' stratum. That proposal is WITHDRAWN. It was wrong, and the reason is technical, not cosmetic.
sparse_level_handling.why_the_threshold_was_wrong: A stratified Cox model estimates NO parameters for its strata. The partial likelihood factorises across strata, so a stratum consumes no degrees of freedom. The usual 'too few events per parameter' concern -- which motivates pooling for a COVARIATE -- simply does not apply to STRATIFICATION. A stratum with few events contributes little information; a stratum with zero events contributes a likelihood factor of 1 and drops out. Neither is an estimability failure. The 20-sample threshold was a numerical reflex imported from the covariate case.
sparse_level_handling.what_pooling_would_cost: Pooling forces batch02, batch09 and batch10 -- which have nothing in common except being small -- to SHARE one baseline hazard. That is the precise assumption the sensitivity analysis exists to test, so pooling would conceal exactly the between-batch heterogeneity being probed, and would do so in the three batches where heterogeneity is least observable. The pooled stratum would also be an artefact with no technical provenance: 'small' is not a processing group.

options_compared.1_keep_all_nine_strata: RECOMMENDED. No parameters are consumed; nothing becomes non-estimable; no heterogeneity is concealed. Cost is efficiency, not validity.
options_compared.2_prespecified_pooling_on_counts_and_pro: REJECTED. No technical provenance links the three small batches, so any pooling would rest on sample count alone -- the reflex just rejected. Pooling on provenance would be defensible IF the SDRF documented shared processing; it does not.
options_compared.3_omit_the_stratified_model: HELD IN RESERVE as the pre-registered failure response, not as the design.

sparse_level_handling.RECOMMENDED_RULE: All nine ComBat batches enter as individual strata. NO pooling, by count or otherwise.
sparse_level_handling.estimability_depends_on_outcome_informat: How much information the nine strata actually carry depends on EVENTS PER STRATUM, which is outcome data and was NOT read here. The DESIGN is fixed outcome-blind; its information content can only be measured at execution. This is stated rather than papered over.

prespecified_failure_response.supersedes: the v2.0 rule 'fewer than 50% of events lie in strata that contribute to the partial likelihood', WITHDRAWN by the Phase 9 final audit as logically near-vacuous (every event lies in a stratum containing an event -- itself) and statistically unfounded (50% has no basis, and labels a PRECISION statement as 'estimability')
prespecified_failure_response.principle: declare non-estimability on MATHEMATICAL and NUMERICAL grounds only -- criteria whose DEFINITIONS are outcome-blind -- and report information loss as a continuous diagnostic rather than gating on an invented threshold
declared_non_estimable_if_and_only_if: the stratified fit fails to converge under the declared criteria (log-likelihood change < 1e-9, max 100 iterations), OR
the observed information matrix for beta is singular or not positive definite (numerical rank < number of coefficients), OR
the separation sentinel trips (any |beta| > 10 or SE > 10)
reported_always_never_gated_on: per-stratum count of events with a NON-DEGENERATE within-stratum risk set -- the events that actually generate a comparison
the number of strata contributing at least one such event
convergence status, iteration count, final gradient norm
RISK-SET COMPARISON RETENTION N_strat / N_unstrat (see REPLACEMENT_information_diagnostic) -- descriptive, no threshold
the per-stratum breakdown of risk-set sizes at event times
the stratified and unstratified coefficient estimates with their bootstrap intervals, side by side and unreduced to a ratio
an explicit statement of the limitation beside the estimate

REJECTED_the_squared_SE_ratio.verdict: REJECTED -- not defensible for THIS model
reasons: ESTIMAND MISMATCH. In a stratified Cox, beta is a WITHIN-stratum log hazard ratio; the unstratified beta is a different functional of the data, equal only under homogeneity of the effect AND proportionality of the baseline hazards across strata. Comparing the precisions of two different parameters is not an information statement about either one.

PENALISED SEs ARE NOT NOMINAL. Under P6B-A1 the M2 pathway coefficients are ridge-penalised, and a penalised coefficient's model-based SE does not carry the usual Wald interpretation. lambda is tuned separately in each fit, so the ratio would partly measure a difference in the TUNED PENALTY rather than in information.

NO GUARANTEED DIRECTION. Stratification removes between-stratum comparisons (lowering information) but also removes confounding by stratum (which can lower residual variation). The ratio is therefore not bounded by 1, and a value above 1 is uninterpretable as 'retention'.
It is a ratio of ESTIMATES with its own sampling variability, for which no uncertainty quantification was specified.

REPLACEMENT_information_diagnostic.name: risk-set comparison retention
REPLACEMENT_information_diagnostic.formula: N_strat / N_unstrat, where N_unstrat = sum over events i of (|R(t_i)| - 1) and N_strat = sum over events i of (|R_{s(i)}(t_i)| - 1); R(t) is the risk set at t and R_s(t) the risk set within the event's own stratum
why_it_is_defensible: MODEL-FREE: a combinatorial property of the design and the event times. It requires no fit, no SE, no lambda and no convergence.
BOUNDED BY CONSTRUCTION: R_s(t) is a subset of R(t), so the ratio lies in [0, 1] and the direction is guaranteed.
DIRECTLY INTERPRETABLE: 'stratification retained X% of the risk-set comparisons the partial likelihood could have used'.
It subsumes the single-event-stratum question automatically: an event whose within-stratum risk set is itself alone contributes 0 comparisons, exactly matching its log(1) = 0 likelihood contribution.
limitations_stated_not_hidden: It counts COMPARISONS, not Fisher information. A retained comparison between two subjects with identical covariate vectors is counted but contributes nothing to the information for beta.
It is reported alongside, not instead of, the number of events with a non-degenerate within-stratum risk set.
It says nothing about precision of any particular coefficient, and is NOT a substitute for the reported confidence intervals.
It requires event times, so it is computed only at authorised execution; its DEFINITION is outcome-blind and is fixed here.
REPLACEMENT_information_diagnostic.no_threshold: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. No pass/fail cut-point is placed on it, now or later; a cut-point would reintroduce the arbitrariness the withdrawn 50% rule was removed for.

diagnostics_are_necessary_not_sufficient.statement: The three estimability criteria are NECESSARY conditions for a usable fit. They are NOT sufficient for adequate information or precision.
explicitly: A positive-definite information matrix does NOT prove adequate information or precision -- it proves only that the parameters are locally identified and the Hessian is invertible. A model can pass all three checks and still have confidence intervals too wide to be useful.

A numerical failure is NOT the same thing as a wide confidence interval, and the two are never reported as if they were. A wide interval is a RESULT, reported as such; a numerical failure means there is no result.
A zero-event stratum contributes no event information and MUST NOT be treated as a numerical failure.
A one-event stratum is not automatically informative: whether its event has a non-degenerate risk set is reported, not assumed.

prespecified_failure_response.response_if_declared_not_estimable: the stratified sensitivity model is REPORTED as not estimable on this cohort and the leave-one-batch-out diagnostic stands alone. We do NOT fall back to pooling: a pooling choice made after seeing events-per-stratum would be an outcome-informed design change.
prespecified_failure_response.why_events_per_stratum_is_the_wrong_quan: a zero-event stratum contributes a likelihood factor of 1 and drops out; an event whose within-stratum risk set is itself alone contributes log(1) = 0 -- zero score, zero information -- while still being counted in any naive events-per-stratum tally

interpretation: Agreement between the stratified and primary fits means the result is not driven by processing group. It does NOT mean batch effects are absent: ComBat was applied before deposit, so between-batch variance was removed by construction.
Disagreement is reported as an unresolved limitation, NOT as grounds to adopt the adjusted model.

The two surviving Phase 8B signals are a control-probe effect and a DISPERSION effect. Neither is a location effect, so neither would be addressed by a batch coefficient -- which is a further reason the adjustment is not promoted.
why_never_primary: batch, RNA extraction method and MMR are mutually confounded in this deposit; no analysis of it can separate them
a batch covariate would absorb biological variation, since batch05 is 63.3% dMMR against 14.3% cohort-wide
the deposited matrix is already ComBat-corrected; adjusting again risks removing signal twice
the primary analysis was pre-specified without batch, and changing that after seeing results would forfeit its pre-specified status

decisions.title: Penalisation scope and clinical-predictor scaling
decisions.raised_by: D8D-1 -- standardising the pathway scores exposes the question for the clinical block, which it does not answer
decisions.current_protocol_text: Phase 6B §3.1 specifies 'ridge, lambda tuned inside resampling' for M1 without saying WHICH predictors the penalty applies to
decisions.frozen_status_note: Penalisation scope is NOT a Register A item. A-11 fixes the predictor LIST; A-15 fixes model ROLES; A-17 the resampling. The penalty's scope is protocol text, so Phase 9 may finalise it -- but it changes the 6B draft, so it is raised for approval rather than settled silently.
decisions.problem: Ridge is not scale-invariant. The clinical block is four binaries plus a 2-column age spline basis on the YEAR scale. If they are penalised alongside the scores, the basis columns (values in the tens) carry small coefficients and are barely shrunk, while the binaries are shrunk comparatively hard -- an arbitrary ordering driven by units.
options_considered: A. penalise everything, standardising the clinical block too (including binaries, which is unusual and makes a 0/1 contrast depend on the training fold's prevalence)
B. force-include the clinical block UNPENALISED; penalise only the pathway scores in M2 and only the selected genes in M3
C. leave the scope unspecified (status quo -- not viable, since the implementation must do something)
decisions.recommendation_text: The five clinical predictors (four binaries plus the age spline basis) are FORCE-INCLUDED and UNPENALISED in M1, M2 and M3. The ridge/elastic-net penalty applies ONLY to the pathway scores (M2) and to the candidate genes (M3).
rationale: An unpenalised coefficient is scale-equivariant: the fit is invariant to any linear rescaling of that predictor. Option B therefore makes the clinical scaling question DISAPPEAR rather than answering it with a convention.
M1 is the benchmark. With 6 df against 135-136 events (EPV ~22) a classical unpenalised Cox fit is appropriate and is the natural reference every genomic model is measured against.
It makes delta-C(M2 - M1) attributable to the PATHWAY BLOCK rather than to differential shrinkage of the clinical terms, which is the comparison the protocol is built around.
It is already what the M3 specification assumes ('clinical covariates force-included and unpenalised'), so option B makes the three models mutually consistent instead of M1/M2 differing from M3.

applied_amendment.field: the 'Penalisation' row of the M1 table
applied_amendment.to: the clinical block (four binary covariates and the age spline basis) is FORCE-INCLUDED and UNPENALISED in M1, M2 and M3. The ridge penalty applies only to the M2 pathway scores and the elastic-net penalty only to the M3 candidate genes; lambda (and alpha for M3) are tuned by inner cross-validation inside each training fold. M1 therefore has no penalised term and no lambda to tune.
applied_amendment.consequence_to_state: M1 ceases to be a penalised model; any comparison with the 6B draft text must say so.

audit_findings_phase9_final_audit.nesting: M1 is exactly M2 with the pathway coefficients set to zero, so the models are properly nested. Had the clinical block been penalised with a model-specific lambda, M1 would NOT be the limit of M2 and the nesting would be broken -- this choice is what MAKES the comparison coherent.
audit_findings_phase9_final_audit.clinical_comparability: IMPROVED -- unpenalised in both models, clinical coefficients differ only through genuine adjustment, not through a shrinkage artefact.
audit_findings_phase9_final_audit.molecular_estimand: delta-C(M2 - M1) estimates the gain from adding a SHRUNK pathway block to an UNSHRUNK clinical model. The penalty pulls the pathway coefficients toward zero, i.e. toward M1, so the comparison is CONSERVATIVE for the molecular block. This must be stated whenever delta-C is reported.
audit_findings_phase9_final_audit.complementarity_with_D8D_1: D8D-1 makes the penalty scale-fair across the pathway scores; D9-1 removes the clinical scaling question entirely. Neither alone is sufficient.

limitations_of_the_recommendation: M1 becomes an unpenalised Cox model, so no lambda is tuned for it. That is a change from the 6B draft text and must be stated as such in any comparison with that draft.

Unpenalised clinical terms are not shrunk, so M1's apparent performance carries the usual optimism -- which is exactly what the bootstrap correction estimates, and the uniform shrinkage factor is reported whether or not it is applied.
If a future protocol wished to penalise the clinical block, the scaling question returns and option A's consequences would have to be faced then.

note: Every recommendation is PENDING_USER_APPROVAL. No frozen record was modified. The proposed M2-A2 amendment text is recorded but NOT applied.
